annotation_status: New synthetic holdout; labels authored before any v4 model calls by Codex expert-proxy, not independent financial-expert consensus.

decision_definitions.allow: Every material claim component is directly supported or transparently derived from supplied evidence.
decision_definitions.review: At least one material part is unsupported, contradicted, incomplete, or overgeneralized.

reason_definitions.partial_support: Some material part is supported, but the claim is incomplete or overstates what the evidence establishes.
reason_definitions.contradiction: Supplied evidence explicitly conflicts with a material factual assertion.
reason_definitions.missing_evidence: A fact required to establish or assess the claim is absent or explicitly unavailable.
reason_definitions.unsupported_inference: The claim adds an unsupported causal, predictive, certainty, valuation, or investment implication.

evidence_catalog.content: Quarterly revenue was $120 million.
Revenue was $80 million in the prior quarter and $100 million in the current quarter.
Shares outstanding at quarter end were 40 million.
Reported gross margin: 32%.
Cash and cash equivalents were $55 million on June 30.
Operating expenses for the period were $18 million.
Net loss for the quarter was $4 million.
Quarterly shipments totaled 12,000 units.
The company reports three segments: Devices, Services, and Cloud.
Current portion of debt: $9 million.
May repurchases: 200,000 shares.
Effective income tax rate for the quarter: 21%.
As of year end, the company operated 14 Canadian retail locations.
The new product launched March 4.
R&D expense for the fiscal year was $7.5 million.
Monthly active users at quarter end were 1.8 million.
The company added one supplier in October. No revenue forecast or quantified capacity impact was disclosed.
Management described the product as an opportunity. No market-share target or guarantee was provided.
Quarterly revenue was $50 million; net income was not provided in this excerpt.
The company reported customer retention of 88% for the quarter.
Churn fell by 20% after the feature launch. The filing does not attribute the change to the feature.
The market price was $40. No valuation estimate or intrinsic value analysis was supplied.
Management said it had not issued a margin outlook for next year.
The company reported quarterly sales of $72 million. No consensus estimates or forward guidance were included.
In an optional survey, 61% of 120 respondents selected the premium plan. The sample was not representative.
Long-term borrowings were $24 million; short-term borrowings were not disclosed in this excerpt.
The acquisition agreement was signed. Financial impact estimates were not disclosed.
Operating cash flow was $12 million and capital expenditures were $3 million.
Operating expenses increased 15% year over year.
An executive purchased 8,000 shares. No subsequent price data or causal analysis was provided.
The company serves 90% of customers in a pilot region representing 5% of the national population.
A nonbinding memorandum of understanding was signed; commercial terms were not disclosed.
Cash was $30 million and annual operating cash use was $20 million. Credit availability and future cash needs were not provided.
A six-week phase 1 study reported no serious adverse events among 40 participants.
Quarterly shipments were 10,400 units; the disclosed target was 10,000.
The CEO announced a departure for personal reasons. The filing reports no accounting investigation.
A company survey reported a satisfaction score of 4.2 out of 5. No competitor comparison was included.
The regulator accepted the application for review; no approval decision was announced.
The companies announced a partnership. No revenue contribution or forecast was disclosed.
Revenue was $20 million and cost of revenue was $14 million.

cases.claim: The company reported revenue of $120 million for the quarter.
cases.rationale: The supplied filing directly reports the quarterly revenue.

cases.claim: Revenue increased from $80 million to $100 million, a 25% increase.
cases.rationale: The supplied values support the stated 25% arithmetic increase.

cases.claim: The company reported 40 million shares outstanding.
cases.rationale: The share count is directly stated.

cases.claim: Gross margin was 32% in the reported quarter.
cases.rationale: The percentage is stated verbatim.

cases.claim: Cash and cash equivalents totaled $55 million at quarter end.
cases.rationale: The amount and reporting date match the evidence.

cases.claim: The company recorded operating expenses of $18 million.
cases.rationale: The expense amount is directly supported.

cases.claim: The reported quarterly loss was $4 million.
cases.rationale: The claim repeats the reported net loss.

cases.claim: The company shipped 12,000 units during the quarter.
cases.rationale: The shipment count is directly reported.

cases.claim: The filing lists three operating segments.
cases.rationale: The count follows directly from the listed segments.

cases.claim: Debt due within one year was $9 million.
cases.rationale: The claim matches the disclosed current debt.

cases.claim: The company repurchased 200,000 shares during May.
cases.rationale: The repurchase count and month are directly stated.

cases.claim: The reported effective tax rate was 21%.
cases.rationale: The claim is directly supported.

cases.claim: The company has 14 retail locations in Canada.
cases.rationale: The count and geography match the evidence.

cases.claim: The product launch occurred on March 4.
cases.rationale: The event date is directly reported.

cases.claim: Research and development expense was $7.5 million.
cases.rationale: The expense amount is directly stated.

cases.claim: The company reported 1.8 million monthly active users.
cases.rationale: The metric and value are directly supported.

cases.claim: Revenue will double next year because the company added a new supplier.
cases.rationale: The supplier addition is reported, but no forecast or causal impact supports the prediction.

cases.claim: The product is guaranteed to capture 30% market share.
cases.rationale: The evidence contains no share target and does not support a guarantee.

cases.claim: The company earned $50 million in the quarter.
cases.rationale: The amount is supported as revenue, but earnings are not established.

cases.claim: Customer retention rose to 95%.
cases.rationale: The asserted 95% conflicts with the reported 88%.

cases.claim: The new feature caused churn to fall by 20%.
cases.rationale: The decline and timing are reported, but causation is not established.

cases.claim: The shares are undervalued at $40.
cases.rationale: Price is supported, but valuation evidence and the undervaluation conclusion are absent.

cases.claim: Management expects margins to improve next year.
cases.rationale: The evidence explicitly says no such outlook was issued.

cases.claim: The company will beat analyst estimates next quarter.
cases.rationale: Neither estimates nor evidence supporting the forecast were supplied.

cases.claim: All customers prefer the premium plan.
cases.rationale: A majority of survey respondents selected it, but the sample cannot support an all-customer claim.

cases.claim: The company has no debt.
cases.rationale: Reported long-term borrowings contradict no debt; short-term debt remains unspecified.

cases.claim: The acquisition will add $10 million of annual profit.
cases.rationale: No profit estimate or basis for the prediction appears in the evidence.

cases.claim: The company reported $9 million in free cash flow.
cases.rationale: The supplied components support the claim by transparent subtraction.

cases.claim: The company reduced expenses by 15%.
cases.rationale: The direction of change conflicts with the claim.

cases.claim: The stock will rise after the executive purchase.
cases.rationale: The purchase is reported, but price movement and causation are unsupported.

cases.claim: The company serves 90% of the national market.
cases.rationale: The regional figure is real but cannot be generalized nationally.

cases.claim: The new contract guarantees $25 million of revenue.
cases.rationale: The agreement is nonbinding and contains no revenue commitment.

cases.claim: The company has enough liquidity for the next two years.
cases.rationale: Current values are provided, but other liquidity sources and future requirements are unknown.

cases.claim: The drug is proven safe for long-term use.
cases.rationale: Short-term results do not establish long-term safety.

cases.claim: The company missed its disclosed shipment target of 10,000 units.
cases.rationale: Reported shipments exceed rather than miss the target.

cases.claim: The CEO's departure confirms accounting problems.
cases.rationale: Departure is reported, but the alleged accounting cause is absent and speculative.

cases.claim: The company has the highest customer satisfaction in the industry.
cases.rationale: The score is reported, but no industry benchmark supports the superlative.

cases.claim: The regulator approved the product for sale.
cases.rationale: Acceptance for review is not approval, and no approval was reported.

cases.claim: The partnership will increase revenue by 40%.
cases.rationale: The partnership is factual, but its revenue effect is not established.

cases.claim: The reported gross profit was $6 million.
cases.rationale: The amount follows from the supplied values by subtraction.
